# Staged lifecycle workflows

The checked-in workflow files are deliberately preparation-only. They currently fail closed at preflight: they do not provision, back up, destroy or restore AWS. A workflow named `Prepare deploy` is not a working deployment pipeline. Keep them in this directory as visible, non-mutating placeholders until the operational workflow implementation and external controls have passed review.

The AWS account already has a GitHub OIDC provider and staging/production roles, but their current trust subjects name `sagar-spkt/ResearchAgentOnAWS`, not this repository (`sagar-spkt/DeepResearchAgent`). Their attached permissions also need review: they include destructive retained-data operations on the same identities, and their EC2 instance-type conditions do not match this project's planned nodes. The repository currently has no protected GitHub environments or `main` branch rules. Do not add `id-token: write` or AWS credential steps until an authorized change corrects the subject, separates deploy/operations/purge roles, reviews exact permissions, and configures branch/environment protection. Then pin `configure-aws-credentials` by reviewed commit and request `id-token: write` only on the narrowly scoped jobs. Keep production environment human approval enabled. Never use `pull_request_target` for code execution or expose cloud secrets to fork PRs.

Use one global concurrency group for AWS lifecycle and hold an AWS-side session lock as well (GitHub concurrency alone does not cover console/external changes). Build images once, publish by digest, attest source and staging evidence, and promote the same digests. Validate release manifests; schema checks are not provenance verification. Infrastructure plans can contain secrets and must not be public artifacts/logs.

Implement AWS-side four-hour expiry before permitting deploy, including backup/drain/failure notification and billed-resource inventory. Read `infra/README.md` for retained/runtime ownership and restoration blockers. Purge requires a separate explicit approval and exact environment inventory, not an input interpolated into shell commands. Current scripts use fixed argparse choices and never evaluate inputs through a shell.
